source_review.notes: Reviewed all ten structured references. Formal foundations were checked against Boehm/Adve, Batty et al., Alglave et al., and Herlihy/Shavit. Current claims were checked against the current C++ atomic draft, Java SE 26 JLS and VarHandle API, Rust 1.98.0 atomic Ordering documentation, the current Go memory model and sync/atomic documentation, and current Arm/Intel manuals. Language interfaces and release-sequence scope are explicitly kept distinct.

evidence: Definitions and Notation defines sb, rf, sw, hb, mo_x, W, S, L, and R before using the formal publication path.
The transitive-closure expression hb=(sb union sw)^+ and event arrows are used consistently with the prose definitions.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation, event direction, carrier identity, and conditional synchronizes-with premises were checked; source relations are not conflated with wall-clock or hardware order.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/CONPAR-027/report.json records four events and three positive edges, with positive payload reachability true.
Removing the release-to-acquire synchronizes-with edge independently recomputes both old-value synchronization and payload reachability as false.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The executable graph counts and reachability outcomes were manually recomputed from the two adjacency matrices and match exact stdout.

evidence: W sb->S, S sw->L, and L sb->R re-derive W hb->R by transitivity.
When L reads initialization rather than S, removing S sw->L breaks every cross-thread path from W to R.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Both positive and negative hb derivations were recomputed from the definitions; no conclusion relies on same-location or elapsed-time intuition.

evidence: Reviewed old-value observation, early publication, wrong carrier, failed CAS, split RMW semantics, fence pairing, intervening modification, and transitive relay.
Reviewed one-time versus repeated generation, generation wrap, premature reclamation, cross-language mismatch, weak architectures, MMIO/DMA, durability, and safety-critical transfer.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Adversarial review spans values, relations, reuse, lifetime, compilation, hardware, device, and persistence boundaries.

evidence: The publication invariant requires complete initialization sb-before release and matching acquire/generation before every protected read.
The reusable-slot state machine separates EMPTY, WRITING, READY, and READING with generation and ownership; publication and lifetime obligations remain separate.
invariant_checking.notes: The chapter preserves the protected-payload invariant only under explicit carrier, reads-from, generation, ownership, and lifetime assumptions.

evidence: The message-passing proof was reviewed edge by edge: producer sb, reads-from-conditioned sw, consumer sb, then hb transitivity.
Negative cases each remove or reverse one necessary premise rather than asserting that acquire/release is globally ineffective.
proof_review.notes: The proof establishes source-level ordering of stated CPU memory events only and does not overclaim snapshot, lifetime, progress, device visibility, or durability.

evidence: Definitions explicitly identify source-level semantics and the exact conditional premise for sw.
The executable model says it stipulates edges and lists formal weak-memory, release-sequence, target, lifetime, device, and durability limitations.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Formal implication, design guidance, deterministic graph evidence, and empirical mapping/performance claims are distinctly labeled.

evidence: python3 tools/verify_snippets.py CONPAR-027 passed the single deterministic graph snippet with exact output and empty stderr.
Assembly, architecture cost, stress results, and hardware behavior are described as target-specific evidence rather than source-model proof.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The model demonstrates graph closure only; it does not execute atomics or establish an allowed-execution theorem.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed separation of atomicity, ordering, reads-from, coherence, publication, lifetime, progress, device visibility, and durability. Acquire/release directionality, conditional synchronization, RMW halves, release-sequence scope, fences, and transitivity are conceptually consistent.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed C++, Rust, Java, and Go API distinctions; carrier/generation design; failed-CAS ordering; reuse/lifetime; preference for higher-level primitives; target assembly and litmus validation; MMIO/DMA warnings; observability; and safety-critical review boundaries.

pedagogical_review.notes: The one-page sheet supplies a dense retrieval target, the exposition builds one graph from first principles, ten examples cover independent failure mechanisms, and five exercises progress from definitions through derivation, diagnosis, design, and unfamiliar hardware transfer with complete answers.

limitations: Internal authoring and verification evidence only; no named external academic, language-standards, practitioner, hardware, controls, clinical, avionics, regulatory, cybersecurity, or functional-safety review is claimed. The Python graph does not execute a weak-memory model or establish target, device, durability, lifetime, or deployment correctness.
